message.content:
In Christian theology, the central figure is Jesus Christ, who is regarded as the incarnate Son of God and the fulfillment of Old‑Testament prophecy. While Jesus is not typically called a “prophet” in the same sense as the Hebrew prophets, he is seen as the ultimate revelation of God’s will.

Beyond Jesus, the Bible contains many prophets—both from the Old Testament (e.g., Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel) and the New Testament (e.g., John the Baptist, who is explicitly called a prophet). These figures are highly respected for their role in conveying God’s messages, guiding the people of Israel, and foreshadowing the coming of Christ.

So, while Jesus is the focal point of Christian faith, several prophets are also considered pivotal in the biblical narrative. The importance of each prophet can vary depending on theological tradition and individual interpretation.
